brief.headline: Pre-Market Briefing: Nifty Eyes Cues as Global Tech Rallies and BPCL Approves Complex
brief.summary: Indian equities head into the session following a sharp correction in the previous session, with global risk sentiment buoyed by strong tech gains on Wall Street and falling crude prices. Key corporate developments include BPCL's massive refinery approval and ongoing Tata boardroom litigation.

takeaways.text: BPCL has approved a massive Rs 1,26,656 crore investment for an integrated refinery-petrochemical complex in Andhra Pradesh.
The Bombay High Court refused interim relief to Tata trusts, allowing the Tata Sons board meeting to proceed on Monday.
Public sector banks posted a 17% growth in H1 FY27, with aggregate net profit surging past Rs 1.09 lakh crore by September 30, 2026.
Global markets rallied overnight, led by strong tech gains on Wall Street and S&P 500 rising 1.60%, while Brent crude dropped 3.98% to 90.84.
Nasscom warns that AI could shrink traditional software maintenance and call centre markets while opening new IT growth opportunities.
Zee Entertainment announced a buyback of up to 65.93 million equity shares at Rs 91 apiece through the tender offer route.

sections.india: State-owned BPCL has greenlit a Rs 1,26,656 crore investment for a new refinery-petrochemical complex in Andhra Pradesh. Meanwhile, public sector banks reported robust numbers with aggregate net profit crossing Rs 1.09 lakh crore for the first half of FY27. Tata Sons and Tata Trusts face continued legal scrutiny as the Bombay High Court declined interim relief ahead of the crucial board meeting.
sections.world: Global equity markets ended the week on a strong footing, with US indices including the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posting solid gains driven by technology strength. Brent crude fell sharply by 3.98% to 90.84, offering macroeconomic relief to oil-importing economies like India. Meanwhile, European markets such as the FTSE 100 posted strong weekly gains supported by rallies in banks and miners.
sections.tech: Nasscom highlighted that artificial intelligence could disrupt and shrink traditional IT maintenance and call center markets, while creating new avenues for Indian tech firms. In hardware, HP launched its OmniBook Ultra 16 in India at Rs 5,49,999 targeting local AI workloads. Concurrently, big tech firms face growing friction as OpenAI accused Apple of undermining its supplier relationships.
